title: Embed API p99 reduction via cooperative batching, kernel dispatch tuning, and jitter analysis
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency (p95/p99) for the Embeddings endpoint without increasing median latency or token cost. Approach combines a jitter-aware cooperative micro-batching scheduler, kernel dispatch parameter tuning for small-batch efficiency, and targeted analysis of latency cliffs caused by long-running kernels and noisy upstream clients. This ticket coordinates experiments, an internal perf harness, kernel parameter sweeps, and a staged rollout with fallback to current behavior.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for 512-token embedding requests reduced from baseline (~240ms) to <= 120ms on standard 40GB GPU profile in internal perf cluster
median latency unchanged (+/- 5ms) and per-token cost <= baseline cost + 5%
No regressions observed on batch-heavy workloads (QPS >= 400) during 48h soak run
Staged rollout with automatic rollback if p99 increases by >10% or error-rate >0.5%
tasks: Build jitter-aware cooperative micro-batcher in runtime (scheduler changes + metrics)
Implement adjustable kernel dispatch knobs (tile size, concurrency cap) and expose via config
Create perf harness to reproduce tail events (synthetic jitter + skewed sequence lengths)
Run parameter sweep across representative models/quantizations and capture traces
Integrate fallback policy: disable coop-batching for sessions with >X% backpressure
Create rollout plan and dashboard panels (p50/p95/p99, error-rate, throughput, cost)
technical_notes: Cooperative micro-batching: workers yield after processing N tokens or M ms to allow urgent small requests to be batched; avoids monopolizing GPU when a single large request would block latency-sensitive small requests
Jitter-aware scheduling: measure incoming inter-arrival distribution per route and adapt the batching window dynamically (0-10ms) using EWMA of inter-arrival times

Kernel tuning focus: reduce kernel latency for small batch sizes by lowering occupancy and improving SM utilization; experiment with smaller tile sizes and fewer warps per block for short-sequence kernels
Tail-cliff mitigation: detect long-running kernel launches (duration > threshold) and slice them into sub-kernel dispatches where safe; add lightweight preemption check in runtime scheduler
Rollback safety: feature flag + canary sampling (0.5% traffic) with automatic rollback triggers based on SLOs
benchmarks: Baseline (internal standard cluster, 40GB A100 equiv): p50=18ms p95=86ms p99=238ms for 512-token batched requests (QPS 300, mixed seq lengths)
Target: p99 <= 120ms while keeping p50 within +/-5ms and per-token cost within +5%
Early experiment (cooperative batching + kernel knob set A): p50=20ms p95=72ms p99=135ms (QPS 320) — promising but edge cases remain for long tail with noisy clients
Parameter sweep artifacts: see artifact links for full CSVs and plots
test_plan: Unit tests for scheduler logic and config parsing
Integration test in perf cluster with synthetic traffic generator (variable inter-arrival jitter profiles)
48h soak with production-like traffic (replay) and canary segment monitoring
A/B comparison against control for cost, p99, error-rate, and throughput
Run regression suite on other endpoints (chat/generate) to ensure no cross-endpoint interference
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind runtime config; default off
Internal perf cluster validation -> dogfood cluster canary (0.5% traffic) for 24h
Increase canary to 5% for 24h with alerting on p99>baseline*1.1 or errors>0.5%
Progress to 25% and then 100% over 72h if no alerts
Automated rollback via orchestration if alert conditions hit
